source_sequence_verbatim: Arrival/retrieval linked to previous careers learning → I Do: explain/model my route map — plan a and plan b with concrete examples → We Do: guided sorting/annotating/scenario discussion → You Do: Model two routes to the same job; students use cards/templates to create Plan A/B; identify one deadline/action; share privately with staff for accuracy check. → 1:1/whole-class review → exit check and add evidence to Careers Portfolio.
timing: Find earlier work and one useful clue; note missing evidence honestly.
Teach route, Plan A, backup and action; model two routes to the same job.
Match route cards and turn a vague wish into a clear action; private hinge.
Choose B or C, or use own generic goal; make Plan A/B and one action.
Private accuracy check, feedback reply and six-outcome portfolio grid.

routes.Supported: Offer two route cards and one instruction at a time. Keep model A, pictures, word bank and frames. Learner chooses or orders the routes and an action using voice, pointing, aid, typing or exact scribe. Log any supplied answer.
routes.Independent: Use B or C, or a self-chosen generic job. Keep normal aids and the model. Create two distinct routes to the same goal and one clear next action. Check unknown facts with an adult.
routes.Aspire: Explain when the backup could help or compare one feature of the routes. Keep a concrete action and usual access. No extra public talk or personal disclosure required.

colour_blind_safe: Pictures, captions, words and marks carry meaning; no colour-only states.
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, route cards, example histories and recap clues are invented and generic. Pictures are symbols, not real people or places. Actual learner work, route choices, dates and encounter modes are recorded honestly. No named provider, employer, organisation, person, place, product or platform.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Pass, pause and supported return are available. No names, private grades, address or family finances requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Evidence Sheet page 2 has blank Type instead fields for either task or an own generic goal. Save through usual routine with lesson code/work reference and show privately. Book, voice, aid or exact scribe also valid. Scribe reads back and permits correction. Log normal access separately from supplied answers.
worked_example_and_fade: Model A has course then work, or paid apprenticeship then work. Both aim at food service assistant. Check: A two different routes or B the same route twice? Key A. Show the different starting steps if unclear. Keep words and model; fade only answer cues.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: one route at a time, reduced choices, pictures, word bank and frames. Communication and Interaction: rehearse, wait, use normal aid and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable chunks, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: clear print, seated or quiet access, no colour-only meaning. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 offer scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only, then return task.
misconceptions: Plan B is not failure or a lesser person’s route. It is a useful alternative. Two job names alone are not two routes to one goal. A training card is not a real offer. Unknown entry needs remain unknown. One NS targets a missing route or vague action; retain first response and reply. VF, WS, I, NS, //, ?, E and R apply. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.

assessment: Exact source evidence: Personal route map with Plan A/B and next action. Shown for Week 6: same goal, distinct viable-in-the-scenario routes and a concrete action. Assess the construction, not a preference, real eligibility or a prediction of future success.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Tuesday 9 February 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · BUILD · up to five learners · Spring 1 Week 6 · assessing week
Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term, 4 January–12 February. Source N21 S: assessing. Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Students build a realistic route to a preferred future and identify an alternative.
I can create a Plan A and a backup Plan B with the next step I need to take.
Focus: My route map — Plan A and Plan B
Source: BUILD Careers, physical row 21 / Spring 1 row 6, E21–N21.

Two different routes can lead towards the same job. Plan A is a first choice; Plan B is a useful backup if plans change. Neither is a promise of entry or work. One next action makes the map usable. Check real requirements and available support with a trusted adult before a real decision.

Show one job goal, two distinct routes towards it and one concrete next action. Include help and a time or review point. A sensible information check is a valid action. Preference and private circumstances are not graded.

Gather each learner’s career story, three-options grid, apprenticeship fact card, requirement-match card and encounter record. Use anonymous work references. Note absent work; never fill gaps from a model. Cards provide invented recap examples for access and new responses only. Books, normal aids, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet ready. Confirm private help and pause/return.
This helps me keep a first choice and a backup, then ask for the help or facts needed for my next step.
Find earlier work and one useful clue; note missing evidence honestly.
Teach route, Plan A, backup and action; model two routes to the same job.
Match route cards and turn a vague wish into a clear action; private hinge.
Choose B or C, or use own generic goal; make Plan A/B and one action.
Private accuracy check, feedback reply and six-outcome portfolio grid.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes, as I21. Processing and short pauses included. Slides 7 and 8 share the 23–35-minute window.

0–5: find one clue from prior work, such as training, support or a requirement to check. Staff pre-check the portfolio before the lesson to allow a brief review at the end. 5–9: teach route, backup and action. 9–13: model A, two routes towards food service work and an entry-check action. Point to the job at both ends. Check that the routes differ. The example is invented, not a learner answer.

13–19: match course route and paid apprenticeship route to the same goal. Use recap Card 4 to link earlier work: careers can change; routes differ; apprenticeships mean paid work with training; strengths and next steps; questions and honest encounter records. Improve “find out” to a specific question with help and a check time. 19–23: private hinge and parallel check; re-model if needed.

23–35: choose B stockroom or C garden, or an own generic goal. In a book, make Plan A and a different Plan B towards the same job. Add one concrete action, help and when to check it. The card order is mixed; learner selects/labels the first and backup routes. Keep actual route choices and response; a copied adult model is supported evidence, not independent thinking. Check privately for accurate earn-and-learn meaning and unknown entry facts.

35–38: each learner shows the map privately; ask which step they will take next. Give one NS and keep the reply. 38–40: add the map and update the pre-checked six-outcome grid from actual evidence. Record missing work or a pass as not yet seen. If more checking is needed, record follow-up; do not rush six new performances into the exit.

Offer two route cards and one instruction at a time. Keep model A, pictures, word bank and frames. Learner chooses or orders the routes and an action using voice, pointing, aid, typing or exact scribe. Log any supplied answer.
Use B or C, or a self-chosen generic job. Keep normal aids and the model. Create two distinct routes to the same goal and one clear next action. Check unknown facts with an adult.
Explain when the backup could help or compare one feature of the routes. Keep a concrete action and usual access. No extra public talk or personal disclosure required.

Model A has course then work, or paid apprenticeship then work. Both aim at food service assistant. Check: A two different routes or B the same route twice? Key A. Show the different starting steps if unclear. Keep words and model; fade only answer cues.

Main: a map has Plan A only. A it is complete; B it needs a different backup and a clear next action. Key B. Parallel: “I will find out” is vague. A ask an adult about entry by Friday and keep the reply; B wait with no check. Key A. Re-model a missing element, then recheck privately. Pass is unobserved.

Cognition and Learning: one route at a time, reduced choices, pictures, word bank and frames. Communication and Interaction: rehearse, wait, use normal aid and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable chunks, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: clear print, seated or quiet access, no colour-only meaning. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 offer scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only, then return task.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Pass, pause and supported return are available. No names, private grades, address or family finances requested.

Evidence Sheet page 2 has blank Type instead fields for either task or an own generic goal. Save through usual routine with lesson code/work reference and show privately. Book, voice, aid or exact scribe also valid. Scribe reads back and permits correction. Log normal access separately from supplied answers.

Exact source evidence: Personal route map with Plan A/B and next action. Shown for Week 6: same goal, distinct viable-in-the-scenario routes and a concrete action. Partly: one element missing or unclear. Not yet seen: insufficient evidence, missing work or pass; comment which applies. Record own generic goal or invented practice mode. Assess the construction, not a preference, real eligibility or a prediction of future success.

Evidence Sheet pages 3–4 carry all six exact G16–G21 outcomes as a tick-and-comment grid. Tick one state per outcome: Shown, Partly or Not yet seen. Add work reference/date, what it shows and access or content prompts. Review actual earlier work; source N20 F + S stays mixed and N21 S assessing. An absent encounter record stays missing/pending; staff role-play is labelled practice. New recap responses get a new date and do not prove a real visit occurred.

Plan B is not failure or a lesser person’s route. It is a useful alternative. Two job names alone are not two routes to one goal. A training card is not a real offer. Unknown entry needs remain unknown. One NS targets a missing route or vague action; retain first response and reply. VF, WS, I, NS, //, ?, E and R apply. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.

Bank route map and six-outcome grid in Careers Portfolio; offer to Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping. Keep concerns out of shared evidence; listen calmly, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures. Only Week 6 authored. BUILD Careers Spring 1 complete; await the full LAUNCH Careers Week 1 brief after acceptance. Further GROW Careers paused.

Careers · BUILD · Spring 1 Week 6 · 8–12 February · up to five learners
Theme: Resilience & Change · assessing week · source N21 S
Students build a realistic route to a preferred future and identify an alternative.
I can create a Plan A and a backup Plan B with the next step I need to take.
My route map — Plan A and Plan B
Personal route map with Plan A/B and next action. Evidence Sheet includes six exact outcomes in a tick-and-comment grid; review actual half-term outputs, including any missing/pending evidence.
Retrieve earlier work and one useful clue.
Teach words and model two routes to the same job.
Guided matching, action planning and private hinge.
Choose B/C or own generic goal; make Plan A/B and an action.
Private accuracy check, feedback reply, portfolio grid.

Supported default; pictures, two task choices, short steps, pre-taught words and usual aids. Book, typing or exact scribe. No public questioning or disclosure. Private help: trusted adult or school’s help route. Where this leads: a first choice, backup and a useful next step. No named provider, employer or place. Physical row 21, Spring 1 row 6.
Use your book or the blank typed page. Pick stockroom work or garden work. You may use your own job goal with an adult. No names.
Write the job you aim for. Plan A is your first route. Plan B is a different backup route to that same job. Use the cards and the work you kept.
Write one thing you can do next. Who can help? When will you check it? You may ask an adult to help check an entry need. Keep unknown facts as questions.
Use one clue from your story, options grid, paid-work-and-training card, skills check or talk record. Show the work to an adult. If work is missing, say so. A practice card can help you try again.
Show Plan A, Plan B and your action to an adult. Keep your first try. Make one change after feedback and show your reply. A backup is a useful way to cope with change.
Ask a trusted adult or use the school’s help route. You may point to HELP, pass, pause and return. Keep private details out of this map.
Blank route record for either choice or your own generic job. Use your words, aid or an exact scribe. No names.
Plan A route and where it leads
Plan B route and where it leads
Clue from earlier work and reference
When I will check the step
One next step and my reply
Save in the usual way with the lesson code and work reference. Show an adult in private. A book is also fine.
Staff record. Use actual work. Tick one state per row. Add date, work reference, what it shows and help given. Leave missing work visible.
1  I can put a simple career story in order and identify where someone adapted to change.
2  I can name at least three next-step options: college/sixth form, apprenticeship/training and employment with training/support.
3  I can explain that an apprenticeship combines paid work with training and identify one thing I would need to apply.
Weeks 1–3: career story and coping note; three-options grid; paid-work-and-training fact card.

Shown: evidence covers the outcome with access recorded. Partly: some parts shown. Not yet seen: missing, pending, pass or not shown yet; say which. Never count an adult model as the learner’s independent work.
A practice talk does not prove a real visit. No total score or grade for a preference. Add one next step and a check time where needed.
Staff record. Use actual work. Tick one state per row. Add date, work reference, what it shows and help given. Leave missing work visible.
4  I can identify one requirement I already meet and one thing I may need to work on.
5  I can ask a prepared question and record whether the option could suit me.
6  I can create a Plan A and a backup Plan B with the next step I need to take.
Weeks 4–6: requirement and next-step card; dated real/practice/pending talk record; Plan A/B route map and action.

Shown: evidence covers the outcome with access recorded. Partly: some parts shown. Not yet seen: missing, pending, pass or not shown yet; say which. Never count an adult model as the learner’s independent work.
A practice talk does not prove a real visit. No total score or grade for a preference. Add one next step and a check time where needed.
I can create a Plan A and a backup Plan B with the next step I need to take.

Goal food service assistant. Course with food tasks then work with training/support, or paid food service apprenticeship with training then food service work. Both aim at the same goal and start differently. Action: by Friday 12 February ask an adult to help check course entry. No real entry fact or offer is invented. The support clue is from the invented practice talk, not a real visit.

B: college work-skills course then stockroom work with support, or paid stock-handling apprenticeship with training then stockroom work. C: college plant-care course then garden work with support, or paid plant-care apprenticeship with training then garden work. Either route can be A or B; assess distinct routes and accuracy, not preference. An own generic job is valid after staff checks the route logic.

Valid: ask an adult to help check one entry need by Friday and keep the answer; practise a named skill with a model at the next check. Vague: find out, try harder, get a job. Help learner specify action, help and check time without inventing real admissions deadlines. Friday 12 February is a lesson action review date only.

Model A: two different routes. Main B: add a different backup and clear action. Parallel A: ask about entry by Friday and keep the reply. Re-model missing element; recheck privately. Pass is unobserved.

W1: ordered career story, change point and coping note. W2: at least three route types named, retaining the full source outcome. W3: paid work plus training and one application need. Look at actual work and recorded prompts. A recap response may give new evidence dated today; it is not proof earlier work was completed.

W4: one evidenced strength/requirement and a next step to work on; unknown personal qualifications stay unknown. W5: learner-selected or constructed question asked through the usual mode and suitability reflection. Keep real, staff practice and pending labels; practice does not establish an actual provider attended. W6: two routes to one goal plus a concrete action, privately checked for accuracy.

Six exact G16–G21 outcomes appear on Evidence Sheet pages 3–4. Tick Shown, Partly or Not yet seen and comment on actual work reference/date, coverage and access/content cues. If missing, pending or passed, state that. No total score or invented evidence. A normal aid does not invalidate an outcome; adult-supplied thinking must be logged. No grade for a yes/maybe/no preference.

Shown: same job goal, two different plausible scenario routes and specific next action. Help and time/check make the action usable. Partly: one element unclear/missing. Not yet seen: no sufficient response; distinguish absence/pass from observed difficulty. Keep first try, one NS and reply. Use another short private check if needed.

Supported default with pictures, word bank, frames and one instruction at a time. Two task choices B/C; own generic goal optional. Independent retains usual aids. Aspire compares a feature or explains backup use. Book, voice, sign, aid, typing or exact scribe valid. Read back and permit correction. No public questioning or forced private account. Plan in any language.

Confirm an available trusted adult and school help route. Learner can point to HELP, pass, pause and return. Listen calmly, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures. Keep concerns outside shared work. No names, real grades, address or family finances requested.

E actual evidence banked; R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Add map and six-outcome grid to Careers Portfolio; offer to Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping. All example people, histories, route cards and deadlines are invented classroom examples; actual work records remain honest.
